title: Probability basics and the normal curve

learn.title: Measuring chance
learn.body: The probability of an event is $P=\frac{\text{favourable outcomes}}{\text{all equally likely outcomes}}$. It is always between 0 (impossible) and 1 (certain). The probability that something does not happen is $1-P$.

learn.title: Two dice
learn.body: What is the chance that the sum is 7?

learn.title: Independent events
learn.body: If one event does not affect the other, multiply: $P(A\text{ and }B)=P(A)\cdot P(B)$. Two heads in a row: $\frac{1}{2}\cdot\frac{1}{2}=\frac{1}{4}$. For at least one head in 3 flips, use the complement: $1-\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^3=\frac{7}{8}$.

learn.title: The normal curve
learn.body: Many measurements make a bell-shaped curve centred on the mean $\mu$, with spread measured by the standard deviation $\sigma$. About 68% lie within 1 $\sigma$ of the mean, 95% within 2 $\sigma$ and 99.7% within 3 $\sigma$. The z-score $z=\frac{x-\mu}{\sigma}$ counts how many $\sigma$ a value is from the mean.

questions.prompt: What is the probability of rolling an even number on one die? Give a fraction.
questions.explanation: Three of the six outcomes (2, 4, 6) are even: $\frac{3}{6}=\frac{1}{2}$.

questions.prompt: Two dice are rolled. What is the probability that the sum is 7?
questions.explanation: 6 of the 36 outcomes sum to 7, so $\frac{6}{36}=\frac{1}{6}$.

questions.prompt: What is the probability of two heads in two fair coin flips?
The chance of rain is 0.3. What is the chance of no rain?
What is the chance of at least one head in 3 fair flips?
questions.explanation: Only TTT has no head, with probability $\frac{1}{8}$. So the answer is $1-\frac{1}{8}=\frac{7}{8}$.

questions.prompt: Scores have mean 100 and standard deviation 15. About what percent lie between 85 and 115?
questions.explanation: 85 and 115 are 1 standard deviation either side of the mean, which covers about 68%.

questions.prompt: Scores have mean 100 and $\sigma=15$. What is the z-score of 130?
Same scores. About what percent lie above 115?
questions.explanation: 68% lie within 1 $\sigma$, so 32% lie outside, split evenly: about 16% above.
